claims.text: Every genital ulcer is tested; history and examination alone are often wrong.
claims.quote: A diagnosis based only on medical history and physical examination frequently can be inaccurate. Therefore, all persons who have genital, anal, or perianal ulcers should be evaluated.
claims.locator: Diseases Characterized by Genital, Anal, or Perianal Ulcers

claims.text: Ulcer workup: syphilis serology plus darkfield or NAAT of the lesion; HSV NAAT or culture; type-specific HSV serology; H. ducreyi NAAT or culture where chancroid is common.
claims.quote: Specific evaluation of genital, anal, or perianal ulcers includes 1) syphilis serology tests and darkfield examination from lesion exudate or tissue, or NAAT if available; 2) NAAT or culture for genital herpes type 1 or 2; and 3) serologic testing for type specific HSV antibody. In settings where chancroid is prevalent, NAAT or culture for Hemophilus ducreyi should be performed.
claims.locator: Diseases Characterized by Genital, Anal, or Perianal Ulcers

claims.text: HIV testing for everyone with a genital ulcer not known to have HIV.
claims.quote: HIV testing should be performed on all persons not known to have HIV infection who present with genital, anal, or perianal ulcers.
claims.locator: Diseases Characterized by Genital, Anal, or Perianal Ulcers

claims.quote: Additionally, biopsy of ulcers with immunohistochemistry can help identify the cause of ulcers that are unusual or that do not respond to initial therapy.
claims.locator: Diseases Characterized by Genital, Anal, or Perianal Ulcers

claims.text: Vulvar or vaginal lesion that may be malignant, or an unclear diagnosis: biopsy.
claims.quote: Vulvar or vaginal biopsy is performed if a lesion found on examination is potentially malignant or the diagnosis is uncertain.
